figures.subject: THE SECOND NECK

source.title: Of the Second Neck
source.deck: An added route is a claim about every dependency it still retains.
source.fiction: The red road passed the great gate. The traveler reached the little gate below it. In the account this was entered as liberation from gates.
source.caption: A new treatment of the original Closed Neck motif. The red path bypasses gate A and rejoins above gate B. A second, separately marked branch tests a route around B. A blank trial box remains blank; no successful intervention is implied.

pages.title: What the bypass bypasses
paragraphs: [D] A bypass is relative to a named obstruction. If two routes avoid one gate but share another required gate, they are independent of the first gate and dependent on the second. This follows from the stated dependencies; it says nothing about whether either gate is desirable. Some gates carry safety checks, coordination, or rights that the new route still needs to supply.

[H] Institutional reforms are often described by the obstruction they remove rather than the dependencies they leave. A new reporting line may still share the disputed manager's budget. A new review panel may still lack authority to obtain records. These are hypotheses to investigate in an actual case, not universal defects of reporting lines or panels.

[D] The plate has two colors because before-and-after claims need distinguishable records. Black shows the retained arrangement. Red proposes a change. Neither color supplies evidence that anyone can use the changed route. A trial should identify an actor, prerequisites, a task, a deadline, and an observable result. Record failures and shared risks alongside successes.

[V] An objection to a gate can be legitimate even when no workable bypass yet exists. Feasibility and justification are separate assessments. The absence of an alternative does not vindicate harmful authority; disapproval of that authority does not manufacture an alternative.

pages.title: The missing warnings
paragraphs: [D] Consider a hypothetical outage. Alarm recognition, diagnosis, authorization, access, dispatch, and repair can overlap and wait on one another. Timestamps divide intervals; they do not by themselves identify causes. Work before dispatch can be technical; delay after dispatch can be administrative. This edition removes the causal partition that survived in the earlier prose.

[H] A useful intervention might grant technicians standing dispatch authority under specified conditions, while preserving coordination, records, and review. Compare restoration outcomes and mistaken dispatches by severity. A faster dispatch is not a sufficient success criterion if it displaces risk onto field crews or customers. The trial needs an accountable recipient who can change the rule.

[D] Before-and-after results can mislead when incident severity, staffing, or infrastructure changed. A single success cannot isolate the effect of authority. Begin with a small, explicit claim. Keep records that allow a later reviewer to say the bypass worked, failed, or cannot be assessed.

[F] The lower gate is not a final revelation that every reform is futile. It is a reminder to follow the route to its declared destination. The traveler may choose to keep the gate and change its keeper. The drawing has left room for that instruction.

figures.subject: THE HOUSE KEPT IN ABEYANCE

source.title: Of the House Kept in Abeyance
source.deck: A refuge preserves some capacities and selects against others.
source.fiction: The house remained closed to the public. Inside, the books were aired, disputes continued, and a child learned which cupboard held the ink. The census called the house empty.
source.caption: Four different carriers of continuity: records, skills, relationships, and rules. Their maintenance supports are shown separately from the room that shelters them. The outer boundary remains permeable because a refuge can depend on institutions beyond itself.

pages.title: Continuity is selective
paragraphs: [E] Taylor's study of the US women's movement treats abeyance structures as bridges through nonreceptive political periods. Its account includes centralization and exclusiveness among the features of such continuity [H1]. It should not be read as an assurance that hidden or quieter organization is egalitarian. Verification for this edition covered the article's abstract and bibliographic identity, not every historical claim in the full paper.

[D] Continuity can preserve skills, relations, purposes, rules, and exclusions in different proportions. A meeting format can survive while its former participants disappear. A slogan can remain while the skill needed for collective work vanishes. A revived organization can retain a name without retaining its earlier accountability.

[H] The refuge question is therefore twofold: what survives there, and what becomes harder to change because it survived there? The proposed audit records maintenance of the four carriers separately. A fifth record tracks the refuge's dependencies: premises, income, care, legal standing, and any supporting institution. The list must be adapted to the actual case.

[V] People who preserve an organization acquire knowledge and may make sacrifices. Neither fact alone grants them permanent jurisdiction over its future. Conversely, criticism of inherited authority does not erase maintenance labor or supply replacements for it. Both claims belong in the account.

pages.title: Return is an occasion for revision
paragraphs: [H] A resumption charter is a proposed device for deciding what must be reconsidered when an organization becomes active again: membership, decision rights, inherited commitments, and the burden of the upkeep. It cannot pre-authorize the consent of future participants. It can state which decisions remain provisional and how a later challenge reaches someone able to act.

[D] A refuge can buffer one exposure while concentrating another. Keeping all records in one stable room may improve preservation but increase dependence on a single caretaker. Distributing records may reduce one point of loss while increasing the burden of keeping versions legible. There is no universally superior arrangement without hazards, costs, and purposes.

[H] Test a narrow prediction: when a historical group resumes activity, do records of rehearsed skills and revisable rules distinguish its performance better than the mere presence of an archive? Code adverse outcomes as well as returns. Do not select only organizations that survived, then explain survival through whatever they happened to retain.

[F] The child is not offered as the house's rightful heir. The scene records transmission without settling inheritance. In the cupboard another hand has left a list of things the next occupants may refuse.

figures.subject: THE KEEPER OF INTERVALS — ORIGINAL

source.title: Of the Keeper of Intervals
source.deck: Who can renew a capacity may shape which future is available.
source.fiction: They took a vote among the four living plans. No one entered the fifth, whose only reader had been allowed to leave. The vote was unanimous.
source.caption: Four independent clocks: public visibility, retained lesson, identity linkage, and usable authority. Each has its own keeper and renewal point. These are analytical distinctions, not recommended retention durations or a diagram of any living network.

pages.title: The decision before the decision
paragraphs: [D] If a future action requires a capacity, and maintenance determines whether that capacity remains available, maintenance can change the set of future actions without changing the eventual voting rule. This is a conditional consequence of the dependency description. It does not prove a motive in the person who controls the maintenance budget.

[H] A consequential selection may therefore occur before a formal decision: one alternative stays staffed, documented, rehearsed, and intelligible while another becomes expensive or impossible to resume. A later comparison can treat their unequal readiness as evidence of unequal merit. This is proposed selection by maintenance, not proof of covert intent. Record when readiness was lost and who could have renewed it.

[D] This is narrower than saying the keeper controls the future. Other routes may exist; new capacities may be invented; people may act outside a permission structure. The keeper controls particular dependencies under particular conditions. The plate uses several clocks to keep that claim local enough to check.

[E] Ulrich and Reynolds distinguish those involved in a designed system from those affected but not involved, and use boundary critique to expose judgments about inclusion and justification [G2]. Here that question is carried into time: whose later options are affected by today's decision to stop maintaining a capacity?

pages.title: The lesson, the name, and the copy
paragraphs: [E] NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System describes de-identifying reports before database entry and separating the reporting process from enforcement functions, with stated exceptions and limits [N1]. It is an example of retaining lessons while limiting identity exposure. It is not proof that de-identification always prevents reconstruction or that its incentive structure transfers to other institutions.

[D] Visibility, retention, identifiability, and practical access are separate variables. Removing a public trace does not show that every copy disappeared. Preserving a lesson does not require retaining every identifying detail. The proper arrangement depends on purpose, rights, technical constraints, and risks. This book offers no universal retention schedule.

[H] Ask whether a lesson can remain useful after its witness becomes harder to identify, and whether a reviewer can test the lesson without restoring unnecessary identity links. Also ask who can change the policy, who can contest the change, and which residual copies remain outside that policy. These are questions for legitimate system design, not a method for mapping vulnerable people.
[F] The fifth plan did not vote against the others. It could no longer be read. The missing entry makes the tally incomplete as a record of the choice that had actually been made.

figures.subject: THE OPEN INVENTORY

source.title: Of the Open Inventory
source.deck: Preserve the means to revise the inventory itself.
source.fiction: At the end of the catalogue the keeper left an unnumbered shelf. The next keeper put a door there. The third asked who had been using the room beyond it.
source.caption: A working alphabet of twelve marks. Each names a question, not a verdict: state, function, repertoire, clock, reserve, carrier, prerequisite, opening, keeper, trial, standing, and revision. The open spiral assembles none of them into a final seal.

pages.title: What this edition claims
paragraphs: [D] The bounded deductive claim is this: under specified dependency, timing, and resource assumptions, preserving a description of an option is insufficient to establish that the option can be used. The executable specimen makes a small instance exact. Its accuracy as a description of any practical system must be established independently.

[H] The proposed synthesis is that maintenance, access, and institutional authority jointly shape a time-qualified repertoire of actions. The distinctive emphasis is the selection that can occur when some capacities are renewed and others lapse before a formal choice. This is a research proposal with clear predecessors, not a priority claim or a validated general theory.

[D] The cross-domain comparisons remain asymmetric. A fluid construction can establish a reachability statement in a prescribed mathematical model. A biological experiment can establish an observed effect under its treatment. A historical study can support an explanation of particular continuity. None can lend its evidential force to the others merely because a diagram resembles them.

[V] Care, non-domination, and revisability constrain the use of the instrument. They remain ethical commitments, open to argument in their own terms. The device does not derive human standing from usefulness or grant a system unlimited jurisdiction because it can keep itself alive.

pages.title: What would change the book
paragraphs: [H] The audit would lose practical force if ordinary scheduling and review already captured the same dependencies at lower cost. The recovery coding would lose force if readers could not distinguish cases consistently. The maintenance-selection claim would lose force in a case where unmaintained alternatives remained equally usable, or where readiness differences did not affect the relevant decision.

[D] No observation needs to refute the conditional schedule when its assumptions hold. Observations can instead show that the assumptions omit what mattered. This distinction prevents a definitional result from being used as an unfalsifiable empirical theory. The book must not claim to have predicted what it only redescribed after the event.

[F] The twelve marks are an invented notation. Their keyed readings are supplied. Nothing depends on discovering a hidden doctrine, and an attractive line is not a reason to obey it. Readers can use the diagrams, disagree with the commitments, or treat the object as an elaborate joke about administrative esotericism.

[F] The final shelf remains available for a correction the present inventory cannot name. That gesture has no causal power. Someone would still have to build the shelf, maintain the room, and let another person put something there.

Match the approved FORAS drawing hand: fine near-black engraved/pen line, dense cellular and lattice ornament with cream voids, fine stroke bundles, sparse muted slate pockets and tiny ochre details, vertical hanging black lines ending in small dots. Keep the new subject's identity and silhouette specified below.
Ground entirely flat unbleached cream #ede6d4, no texture gradient, vignette, background scene or cast shadow. Figure alone centred, completely visible including extremities and terminal dots; generous empty margin on all sides, about 75-80 percent of canvas height. Fine line art and at most light flat wash. No painted modelling, photographic lighting, glossy reflections or 3D render.
Palette: near-black #161918; exactly ONE red intervention. All red stroke cores must be flat sRGB #a32b24, RGB(163,43,36), no red highlights, shadows, black outline or orange/bright crimson variation; antialias edges only. Muted slate #4f6f7a and a little ochre are the only other hues. Red appears nowhere outside the specified intervention.
No text, letters, numerals, pseudo-writing, captions, watermark, border, page frame or surrounding diagram. Blank book/paper surfaces. No extra figures unless the requested subject is explicitly the Hora-and-Tempus pair. Any handheld or structural frame specified below belongs to the subject, never a border around the image.

NEW SUBJECT — THE CUT KEEPER — GRADUUM III. Input image 1 FORAS is drawing hand and palette ONLY. Input image 2 ORIGINAL MEASURER OF ABSENCES is identity, antler silhouette, bowed posture, careful bearded profile face and EMPTY HANDHELD RECTANGLE ONLY. Preserve those recognisable features, re-render the entire full-length antlered keeper in the series fine cellular-lattice pen register. Remove all typography, page borders, registers, separate details and all red veins/eyes from the old plate. The figure holds an empty black rectangular frame between its two delicate hands, frame centre plain cream. From neck down the body is HALF living stroke bundles/lattice on viewer's left, HALF a clean RULED TABLE on viewer's right: garment and torso turn into open black rows and columns, not lettering. The boundary between organic half and ruled half is ONE SINGLE fine VERTICAL RED LINE running from below neck through the body to hem, red #a32b24; no other red in antlers, eye, hands or frame. Keep the WHOLE FACE organic and detailed, not sliced into a grid. Outer silhouette remains one continuous figure, no separate chart beside it. No text in cells, no numerals, no extra diagrams. Portrait PNG 2:3, target 2048 x 3072 if supported.
figures.qa_notes: Measurer-derived antlered bearded face and empty handheld rectangle preserved; organic left body and ruled right body separated by a red vertical boundary, partly occluded by foreground arm.
